title: User-Friendly Pipelines for Data Analysis
text: turtle R package provides simplified, user-friendly functions common data analysis tasks modelling, dimensionality reduction, visualization. designed support users minimal programming knowledge allowing specify key inputs (e.g., outcome, exposure, covariates etc.) automatically handle underlying code. applicable wide range data types, including epidemiological, ecological, experimental datasets. core functions include: run_linear_models(): Fit linear mixed models (can run single model many models). save_model_output(): Save models summaries (e.g., run_linear_models) computer. extract_model_summaries(): Extract model results run_linear_models(). run_model_diagnostics(): Run plot diagnostics models.

code: library(turtle)  # Example: Does car weight affect fuel efficiency? output <- run_linear_models(   data = mtcars,   outcome = "mpg",   # miles per gallon   exposure = "wt"    # weight of the car )  # View the results output$tidy #> # A tibble: 2 × 9 #>   term        estimate conf.low conf.high std.error  p.value error n_obs   BIC #>   <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> <lgl> <int> <dbl> #> 1 (Intercept)    37.3     33.5      41.1      1.88  8.24e-19 NA       32  170. #> 2 wt             -5.34    -6.49     -4.20     0.559 1.29e-10 NA       32  170. library(turtle)  outcomes <- c("mpg", "disp") exposures <- c("cyl")  output <- run_linear_models(   data = mtcars,   outcome = outcomes,   exposure = exposures )  output$tidy #> # A tibble: 2 × 9 #>   term        estimate conf.low conf.high std.error  p.value error n_obs   BIC #>   <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> <lgl> <int> <dbl> #> 1 (Intercept)    37.9     33.6      42.1      2.07  8.37e-18 NA       32  174. #> 2 cyl            -2.88    -3.53     -2.22     0.322 6.11e-10 NA       32  174. results <- extract_model_summaries(output)  head(results) library(dplyr)  results_cyl <- filter(exposure == "cyl")  results_mpg <- filter(outcome == "mpg") extract_model_summaries(results, p_adjust_method = "fdr") save_model_output(   model_output = output,   file_path = "my_model_results") save_model_output(   model_output = output,   file_path = "just_models",   models_only = TRUE ) load("my_model_results_20250718.RData")

what: Fit Linear or Mixed Effects Models Across Multiple Variable Combinations — run_linear_models
title: Fit Linear or Mixed Effects Models Across Multiple Variable Combinations — run_linear_models
text: function fits linear (`lm`) mixed effects (`lmer`) models across combinations outcomes, exposures, effect modifiers, sensitivity covariates. supports interaction terms, random effects, returns tidy summary model. designed simplify model fitting across many variable combinations consistent covariates random effects. internal testing purposes, hidden `.test_force` argument can passed via `...` simulate interactive, top-level calls. enables reliable testing preview reminder output without relying `interactive()` `sys.nframe()`.

title: Fit Linear or Mixed Effects Models Across Multiple Variable Combinations — run_linear_models
text: data data frame containing variables used model. outcome character vector outcome variable names. exposure character vector exposure variable names. covariates character vector covariate names adjust (e.g., confounders). included models. effect_modifier character vector effect modifiers interact exposure. combinations tested. sensitivity_cov character vector sensitivity covariates include model. combinations tested. random_effects string specifying random effects structure (e.g., "(1 | group)"). `NULL`, linear model used. p_values Logical. `TRUE` (default), uses `lmerTest` compute p-values mixed models. `FALSE`, uses `lme4` without p-values. verbose Logical. `TRUE` (default), prints progress model status messages. return_grid Logical. `TRUE`, attaches model grid attribute returned object.

title: Fit Linear or Mixed Effects Models Across Multiple Variable Combinations — run_linear_models
text: named list model results. element contains: model fitted model object. tidy tidy summary model (term, estimate, confidence intervals, p-values, etc.). residuals Model residuals. formula model formula used. multiple combinations tested, list named using format `outcome&exposure&modifier&sensitivity`. list containing model results. multiple outcomes exposures provided, returns named list results.

title: Fit Linear or Mixed Effects Models Across Multiple Variable Combinations — run_linear_models
code: # Examples  data <- mtcars  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # 1. Run a single model with one outcome and one exposure run_linear_models(data = data,                   outcome = "mpg",                   exposure = "cyl") } # }  # 2. Store the output for a single model model_output <- run_linear_models(data = data,                                   outcome = "mpg",                                   exposure = "cyl") #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = cyl model_output$tidy  # access tidy results #> NULL  # 3. Store output for multiple outcomes and exposures multi_output <- run_linear_models(data = data,                                   outcome = c("mpg", "hp"),                                   exposure = c("cyl", "wt")) #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = cyl #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = wt #> Running model with outcome = hp, exposure = cyl #> Running model with outcome = hp, exposure = wt multi_output[["mpg&cyl"]]$tidy  # access a specific model's tidy results #> # A tibble: 2 × 11 #>   term  estimate conf.low conf.high std.error  p.value error n_obs   BIC formula #>   <chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> <lgl> <int> <dbl> <chr>   #> 1 (Int…    37.9     33.6      42.1      2.07  8.37e-18 NA       32  174. mpg ~ … #> 2 cyl      -2.88    -3.53     -2.22     0.322 6.11e-10 NA       32  174. mpg ~ … #> # ℹ 1 more variable: note <chr>  # 4. Use named vectors for outcomes and exposures outcomes <- c("mpg", "hp") exposures <- c("cyl", "wt") named_output <- run_linear_models(data = data,                                   outcome = outcomes,                                   exposure = exposures) #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = cyl #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = wt #> Running model with outcome = hp, exposure = cyl #> Running model with outcome = hp, exposure = wt named_output[["hp&wt"]]$tidy #> # A tibble: 2 × 11 #>   term   estimate conf.low conf.high std.error p.value error n_obs   BIC formula #>   <chr>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <lgl> <int> <dbl> <chr>   #> 1 (Inte…    -1.82    -67.8      64.2     32.3  9.55e-1 NA       32  353. hp ~ wt #> 2 wt        46.2      26.5      65.8      9.63 4.15e-5 NA       32  353. hp ~ wt #> # ℹ 1 more variable: note <chr>  # 5. Include covariates directly covar_output <- run_linear_models(data = data,                                   outcome = "mpg",                                   exposure = "cyl",                                   covariates = c("wt", "hp")) #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = cyl covar_output$tidy #> NULL  # 6. Include covariates using a named vector covars <- c("wt", "hp") names(covars) <- covars named_covar_output <- run_linear_models(data = data,                                         outcome = "mpg",                                         exposure = "cyl",                                         covariates = covars) #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = cyl named_covar_output$tidy #> NULL  # 7. Include an effect modifier (e.g., interaction term) interaction_output <- run_linear_models(data = data,                                         outcome = "mpg",                                         exposure = "cyl",                                         effect_modifier = "am") #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = cyl, effect_modifier = am interaction_output$tidy #> NULL  # 8. Model with a non-existent variable (graceful failure) error_output <- run_linear_models(data = data,                                   outcome = "mpg",                                   exposure = "not_a_column") #> Running model with outcome = mpg, exposure = not_a_column #> Model failed for formula: mpg ~ not_a_column #> Error: object 'not_a_column' not found  error_output$tidy #> NULL

what: Run Diagnostics on Fitted Linear or Mixed Effects Models — run_model_diagnostics
title: Run Diagnostics on Fitted Linear or Mixed Effects Models — run_model_diagnostics
text: function runs suite diagnostic checks one fitted models (`lm` `lmerMod`). supports parallel processing, customizable diagnostic selection, optional PDF export index summary pages. Designed help users assess model quality identify potential issues outliers, heteroscedasticity, multicollinearity, . summary page provides layperson-friendly explanations diagnostic. Outlier percentages calculated model reported, models removed filtered based values. Parallel processing uses `future::multisession()` automatically resets plan execution avoid side effects.

title: Run Diagnostics on Fitted Linear or Mixed Effects Models — run_model_diagnostics
code: run_model_diagnostics(   models,   diagnostics = c("heteroscedasticity", "outliers", "collinearity", "normality",     "autocorrelation", "random_effects"),   parallel = FALSE,   outlier_threshold = 10,   save_pdf = FALSE,   pdf_path = "model_diagnostics.pdf",   index_labels = NULL,   chunk_size = 100,   readme_url = "https://github.com/drhealy013/turtle" )

title: Run Diagnostics on Fitted Linear or Mixed Effects Models — run_model_diagnostics
text: models single fitted model (`lm` `lmerMod`) named list models. diagnostics character vector specifying diagnostics run. Options include `"heteroscedasticity"`, `"outliers"`, `"collinearity"`, `"normality"`, `"autocorrelation"`, `"random_effects"`. Defaults . parallel Logical. `TRUE`, diagnostics run parallel using `furrr`. Defaults `FALSE`. outlier_threshold Numeric. Percentage threshold used reporting (filtering). Defaults `10`. save_pdf Logical. `TRUE`, saves diagnostic plots PDF. Defaults `FALSE`. pdf_path String. File path saving PDF `save_pdf = TRUE`. Defaults `"model_diagnostics.pdf"`. index_labels Optional character vector labels grouping models index page. chunk_size Integer. Number models per chunk parallel processing. Defaults `100`. readme_url String. URL online guide README explanation. Defaults `"https://github.com/drhealy013/turtle"`.

title: Run Diagnostics on Fitted Linear or Mixed Effects Models — run_model_diagnostics

what: Save Model Output to File with Timestamping and Format Handling — save_model_output
title: Save Model Output to File with Timestamping and Format Handling — save_model_output
text: function saves output `run_linear_models()` compatible list model results `.RData` file. supports saving either full output (including summaries, residuals, formulas) just fitted model objects. function automatically appends date-based timestamp filename (already present), ensures correct file extension, provides overwrite protection. single model object (e.g., `lm`, `lmerMod`) provided, wrapped named list (`model1`) ensure compatibility. Generic lists also accepted, though warning issued input `run_linear_models()`.

title: Save Model Output to File with Timestamping and Format Handling — save_model_output
text: model_output model object list model results, ideally `run_linear_models()`. Must list model object can wrapped list. file_path character string specifying file path save output. `.RData` included, appended automatically. models_only Logical. `TRUE`, fitted model objects (e.g., `lm`, `lmerMod`) saved. useful need re-run predictions diagnostics later. `FALSE` (default), full output saved — including model summaries, residuals, formulas — recommended users. verbose Logical. `TRUE` (default), prints styled messages summarizing save operation suggesting next steps. overwrite Logical. `FALSE` (default), function stop file already exists. Set `TRUE` allow overwriting.

title: Save Model Output to File with Timestamping and Format Handling — save_model_output
text: (Invisibly) list containing: object object saved (either full output model-list). path full file path object saved.
